Q27867914.summary: Along the front of this marble chest, framed by columns, Christ stands at the centre among ten apostles who turn toward him in pairs, many holding scrolls. The gabled lid, carved with overlapping scales like roof tiles, bears at its centre the chi-rho, the monogram formed from the first Greek letters of Christ's name. The whole presents Christ as teacher and Lord surrounded by the college of apostles, an image of the Church gathered around him in hope of eternal life.
facts: According to the museum, the lid did not originally belong to this chest, though it probably also came from Saint-Sernin; an inscription on its back records its reuse in 1754 for the tomb of a Toulouse merchant, Antoine Vigniaux.
In the 1770s the chest decorated the garden of Count Jean Dubarry's town house opposite Saint-Sernin, where it was nicknamed the 'Tomb of Jean-Jacques Rousseau'.

The hole drilled through the middle of the front, visible below Christ, is thought by the museum to have caused the crack that runs through the same spot; the short sides show a shepherd with his sheep and a lion hunt.
Q27867914.notes: POP dates the work to the 4th–5th century (worklist: 4th century). Wikidata's English description calls it 'bronze'; it is marble. The place of manufacture is not stated by the museum; only the findspot (the old 'cemetery of the nobles' at Saint-Sernin) is recorded.
Q27867914.original_title: Sarcophage au Christ, Pierre et Apôtres (Ra 507)
